# Summary of the British National Party Manifesto 2010

The 2010 BNP Manifesto presented a nationalist platform centered on several core themes: immigration restriction, EU withdrawal, anti-Islam policies, and economic protectionism.

## Immigration and Demographics
The manifesto's central concern was halting what it termed the "immigration invasion." It claimed indigenous British people would become a minority within 50 years and proposed stopping all immigration, deporting illegal immigrants, ending asylum claims, and promoting voluntary repatriation with financial incentives. The party proposed repealing the Race Relations Act and abolishing multiculturalism policies.

## European Union
The BNP demanded immediate EU withdrawal, arguing the organization undermined British sovereignty. It claimed EU membership cost £15 billion annually and promised to redirect these funds domestically.

## Counter-Jihad Policies
The manifesto declared Islam "incompatible with Western democracy" and proposed banning the burka, halting mosque construction, prohibiting Muslim immigration, and deporting radical preachers. It linked terrorism to mass immigration and British foreign policy in the Middle East.

## Defence and Foreign Policy
The party advocated withdrawing troops from Afghanistan, increasing defence spending, and pursuing a non-interventionist foreign policy focused solely on British interests. It proposed ending foreign aid entirely.

## Economy
Economic proposals included cutting expenditure on climate change initiatives, EU membership, and foreign aid to reduce national debt. The manifesto supported protectionist trade policies, tariffs on Third World imports, preventing foreign takeovers of British companies, and separating retail from investment banking.

## Welfare and Public Services
The BNP proposed restricting welfare benefits to British citizens who had contributed to the system, implementing "workfare" requirements, and prioritizing British people for NHS services and social housing.

## Other Policies
Additional proposals included restoring grammar schools, renationalizing rail services, opposing climate change science, reintroducing capital punishment for certain crimes, creating an English parliament, and protecting traditional British culture.
